newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes edge higher, paper gains trimmed.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes edge higher, paper gains trimmed.

text.p: Spot North Sea crudes held onto early gains on Wednesday but paper markets lost some of their shine amid uncertainty about the direction of Dated Brent, traders said.
Two Brent cargoes, loading Dec 2-4 and Dec 3-5, traded early at the widely divergent levels of Dec Brent -45 and Dec Brent -33 cents, the latter seven cents above what it fetched Tuesday.

The higher number was seen as a truer reflection of market sentiment and the Jan/Feb intermonth spread jumped to trade as high as +52 cents before easing in late talk to +48/+51 cents, still about five cents up on the day.

Brent CFDs firmed about 10 cents, pulling the market into backwardation with next week's dates talked as high as Jan Brent +2/+5 cents before news of two five o'clockings pushed them back to -1/+4 cents.
The Brents, due to load Dec 5-7, were clocked to British Petroleum and Wall Street trader J. Aron, dealers said.
"The market's looking quite balanced at the moment but it's nothing to get too excited about," said a trader.
Some North Sea grades edged higher with Forties trading at least twice for about Dated Brent +22/+23 cents, compared with trade on Tuesday at +20 cents.
But others, like Statfjord and Ekofisk, remained depressed, traders said.

In the Mediterranean, Urals climbed with Tuesday's deal at Dated Brent -60/65 cents cif Med. Prospects of Black Sea weather delays, upcoming maintenance on the main jetty at Novorossiisk and uncertainty over the December loading programme were combining to lift the differential, traders said.
Negotiations on Syrian and Algerian pricing for December got underway with the respective state oil companies asking for unchanged differentials versus November.
